title: Finite direct image reflects constructibility
statement:
Let $p:Z\to S$ be a
finite morphism of
Noetherian schemes, let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring, and
let $F$ be an etale sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $Z$.
If its direct image $p_*F$ is
constructible, then
$F$ is constructible.

proof.text: Put $G=p_*F$ and $H=p^{-1}G$, in the category of sheaves of modules over the same constant finite ring $\Lambda$. By [prop-constructible-pullback], applied with module values (the category-of-values convention in [def-constructible-constant]), $H$ is constructible. More explicitly, pull back a finite stratification adapted to $G$; its restrictions are finite locally constant module sheaves. Each pulled-back stratum has constructible underlying subset by [lem-pur-scheme-constructible-preimage]. Thus this is precisely the module-sheaf constructibility of [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf], without changing coefficients or passing to the pro-etale site.

source.place: Tag 095G, lemma-pullback-constructible; global finite-partition form Tag 095E, lemma-constructible-quasi-compact-quasi-separated

proof.text: Let $\varepsilon:H=p^{-1}p_*F\to F$ be the counit of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Fix a geometric point $\bar z$ of $Z$ and write $\bar s=p\bar z$. Identify $H_{\bar z}$ with $(p_*F)_{\bar s}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ]. For a germ represented by $a\in(p_*F)(V)=F(V\times_SZ)$ at a pointed etale neighbourhood $(V,\bar v)$ of $\bar s$, that identification sends the germ of $\eta_{p,p_*F}(V)(a)$ at $(V\times_SZ,(\bar v,\bar z))$ to the germ of $a$. The triangle identity $p_*\varepsilon\circ\eta_{p,p_*F}=\mathrm{id}_{p_*F}$ says that applying $\varepsilon$ to this pulled-back section gives $a$ on $V\times_SZ$. Therefore $\varepsilon_{\bar z}$, under the identification, is exactly the restriction-of-germs map $r_{p,\bar z,F}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula-restriction]. Every germ of $(p_*F)_{\bar s}$ has such a representative, so this proves equality of the two maps. That cited finite-fibre formula makes this restriction a product projection and hence surjective. The formula applies to the underlying abelian sheaf; all maps preserve the $\Lambda$-action because they are the module inverse-image adjunction maps. No assumption that $p$ is surjective is used: for each chosen $\bar z$ its fibre contains the specified factor.

source.place: Tag 03Q1, lemma-stalk-pullback (3), germ computation from equation-pullback; Tag 03QP, proposition-finite-higher-direct-image-zero (1)

proof.text: Let $C=\operatorname{Coker}(\varepsilon)$ in the abelian module-sheaf category of [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Cokernels of module sheaves have the underlying abelian-sheaf cokernel (sheafify the sectionwise quotient with its induced $\Lambda$-action). Exactness of geometric stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] gives $C_{\bar z}=\operatorname{Coker}(\varepsilon_{\bar z})=0$ for every $\bar z$, by step 2. Thus the underlying abelian-sheaf map $C\to0$ is an isomorphism on every geometric stalk, hence an isomorphism by [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]. Consequently $C=0$ and $\varepsilon$ is an epimorphism. This applies the conservative-stalk node only to an isomorphism, as its statement requires.

Set $K=\operatorname{Ker}(\varepsilon)\subseteq H$. The scheme $Z$ is Noetherian and $\Lambda$ is finite, so [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-subobjects-noetherian] applies to the constructible $H$ of step 1 and makes $K$ constructible. The inclusion $K\to H$ is now a morphism between constructible module sheaves. By the cokernel clause (1) of [thm-constructible-serre], $\operatorname{Coker}(K\to H)$ is constructible. Since $\varepsilon$ is epic by step 3, the kernel-cokernel identity in the abelian category identifies this cokernel with $F$. The partition and its module trivializations for the cokernel become those for $F$ under this isomorphism, proving the assertion.
